newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-GUD sees mixed 2nd half outlook.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-GUD sees mixed 2nd half outlook.

text.p: Automotive parts and appliance manufacturer GUD Holdings Ltd said on Tuesday its outlook for the second half of the 1996/97 (July-June) year was mixed.
"There is a mixed outlook for GUD's businesses in the second half," GUD Holding said in its first half results statement.

Earlier, GUD reported a 57 percent rise in net profit for the six months to December 31 to A$9.13 million, but this result included a contribution from the recently-acquired lawnmower maker Sunbeam Victa and car filter maker Wesfil.
Earnings per share rose to 17.2 cents from 15.2 cents.
GUD also increased its interim dividend to 9.5 cents per share from 9.0 cents.
GUD Holdings managing director Ian Beynon said the result was achieved despite continuing economic and seasonal difficulties and import competition.
Beynon said softer demand in Australia was evident in the second half of the year.
"At the same time, the integration of Sunbeam Victa had progressed satisfactorily," GUD said.
GUD's Filtration products division recorded slightly lower sales for the first half, but significantly lower profit.
"Sales of automotive filters to the car companies were strong, but segments of the parts and accesories market declined noticeably," Beynon said.
A subdued construction and office equipment market hurt the Security Products Division, GUD said.
GUD's domestic and farm pumps unit had lower sales and margins because of poor climatic conditions.
"Export sales were maintained despite the strong Australian dollar," Beynon said.
Victa Mowers had a very strong first quarter because of favourable seasonal conditions and the release of a new "Mulch or Catch" mower.
"Dry conditions in the second quarter resulted in flat sales for the half but at improved margins," GUD said.
"Sunbeam Rural Products had a disappointing half, with sales and profit lower than expected."
GUD said sales by Sunbeam Appliances in January and February were ahead of budget.

"Victa Mowers, Sunbeam Rural products and Davey Products traditionally experience seasonally lower demand in the second half, although Victa and Sunbeam Rural are undertaking major programmes which should improve results in the first half of 1997/98," GUD said.
"Hot, dry conditions in January and February in southern Australia have also improved Davey's outlook," it said.
"However the Filtration and Security products businesses in Australia are expecting difficult trading conditions for the rest of the year."
GUD said the group was beginning to achieve significant general cost reductions because of the increased size of the group.
"This includes funding and insurance costs, telecommunications, power and raw materials."
GUD's shares were up four cents at A$3.99 at 12.20 (0120 GMT).
